title: Echolume, a game I made in vanilla JS using Claude Code Fable, is live on iOS!
author: MyTech_Vibes
selftext:
**Echolume** went live on the App Store today. It is a one-thumb game that pairs something I find pleasure in, drifting slowly in water, with one of my fears, cave diving (I scuba dive, and avoid caverns like the plague)

You play a small blind creature in a deep-sea cave, and the only way to move is to sing. Tap, and the sound pushes you through the water and lights up the walls around you for a second. The catch is that the hunters hear it too, and they swim to wherever you sang last.

I wanted to see if I could build it mostly using vanilla JS. With Claude's help, apparently that was possible. All art and motion is JS, and the thing I'm most proud of: there are no audio files! All sound is from WebAudio primitives: oscillators, filters and gain envelopes.

Placement needed its own test harness, because I had like 200+ playthroughs where I was catching random objects outside of the "cavern walls". So now there's automation that goes through every level to validate placement before a new build. Claude built this without me being too involved, but I have an agent that ensures this is covered with every build.

I hope you like it! Free on the iOS App Store (with ads because I like to eat)

[https://apps.apple.com/us/app/echolume-sound-light/id6799615320](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/echolume-sound-light/id6799615320)

Feedback welcome! I'll work on features in a couple of weeks
